beats.intro: Now that you know what an equation is, it's time to solve one. [[q]]Solving means finding the value that makes the equation true, by getting the variable alone.
beats.balance: Here's x plus two equals six, on a balance. [[tiles]]The left pan holds one x bar and two unit tiles. The right pan holds six unit tiles. [[goal]]The goal is to get the x bar alone. [[one]]Take two tiles off the left pan only, [[tip]]and the scale tips: the sides are no longer equal. [[both]]Take two tiles off the right pan too, [[level]]and it's level again. [[ans]]Now the x bar balances four tiles, so x is four. [[rule]]Whatever you do to one side, you must do to the other.
beats.inverse: To undo an operation, use its inverse. [[add]]The inverse of adding is subtracting. [[sub]]The inverse of subtracting is adding. [[mul]]The inverse of multiplying is dividing, [[div]]and the inverse of dividing is multiplying. [[ex]]In x minus seven equals twelve, seven is subtracted from x. So add seven to both sides. [[ans]]x equals nineteen. [[check]]Check: nineteen minus seven is twelve. It works.
beats.divide: Now negative six t equals one hundred thirty-eight. [[what]]t is multiplied by negative six. [[inv]]The inverse is dividing by negative six, on both sides. [[ans]]One hundred thirty-eight divided by negative six is negative twenty-three. [[check]]Check: negative six times negative twenty-three is one hundred thirty-eight.
beats.twoStep: Some equations need two steps. [[q]]Take three x plus thirteen equals seven. [[order]]To build three x plus thirteen, you'd multiply x by three, then add thirteen. To undo it, go in reverse: first subtract thirteen, then divide by three. It's like taking off your shoes before your socks. [[s1]]Subtract thirteen from both sides: three x equals negative six. [[s2]]Divide both sides by three: x equals negative two.
beats.dist: With parentheses, distribute first. [[q]]Four times m minus three equals twenty. [[d]]Four m minus twelve equals twenty. [[s1]]Add twelve to both sides: four m equals thirty-two. [[s2]]Divide by four: m equals eight. [[alt]]Another way: divide both sides by four first. m minus three equals five, so m is eight.
beats.both: Sometimes the variable is on both sides. [[q]]Five m minus two equals twelve m minus sixteen. [[move]]Subtract five m from both sides, so the variable is only on the right: negative two equals seven m minus sixteen. [[s1]]Add sixteen to both sides: fourteen equals seven m. [[s2]]Divide by seven: m equals two. [[check]]Check: five times two minus two is eight, and twelve times two minus sixteen is also eight.
beats.story: Equations solve real problems. [[q]]A club has one hundred twenty dollars and sells boxes of cookies for eight dollars each. How many boxes must it sell to reach four hundred dollars? [[eq]]Let b be the number of boxes. Eight b plus one hundred twenty equals four hundred. [[s1]]Subtract one hundred twenty: eight b equals two hundred eighty. [[s2]]Divide by eight: b equals thirty-five. The club must sell thirty-five boxes.
beats.wrap: To solve an equation, [[w1]]simplify each side first: distribute and combine like terms. [[w2]]Use inverse operations to get the variable alone, undoing addition and subtraction before multiplication and division. [[w3]]Always do the same thing to both sides, and check by substituting. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. Find the first step for each equation.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter twenty-five, solving one-variable equations.
